question: How are standardization and min-max normalization different in what they preserve and why they are used?
direct_answer: Standardization centers and rescales by spread; min-max normalization maps values into a fixed range like [0, 1].
expanded_answer: Standardization subtracts the mean and divides by the standard deviation, so the transformed feature has roughly zero mean and unit variance. Min-max normalization instead linearly compresses values into a bounded interval. Standardization is often preferred when a method is sensitive to variance, covariance, or optimization conditioning. Min-max scaling is useful when you want all features in a fixed, bounded range, but it can be more sensitive to outliers because extrema determine the scale.
key_points: Standardization uses mean and standard deviation
Min-max uses minimum and maximum values
common_wrong_ideas: Both methods have the same effect
Min-max scaling is always more robust than standardization
